newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end firmer, palladium weaker.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end firmer, palladium weaker.

text.p: New York precious metals ended higher, apart from palladium, as dealers puzzled over German announcements about the fate of yellow metal held in the mighty Bundesbank vaults.

"The market reacted yesterday when it came out that they might sell some gold, a change of heart for the Germans. But Waigel made it clear they are not going to be selling any gold, just reevaluating it," Scott Mehlman, chief dealer at Credit Lyonnais Rouse said.
German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said Thursday not a single ounce of Bundesbank gold reserves would be sold.
Gold prices dipped late Wednesday and overnight on fears, stemming from a newspaper article, that Germany may sell gold.
COMEX June gold settled 20 cents firmer at $348.40 an ounce, traded $349.30 to $346.70 in largely choppy, erratic dealings. Bullion was at $347.20/$347.70 late afternoon.
Germany's Waigel is trying to fill gaps in his 1997 budget which are threatening to keep the country from qualifying for Europe's single currency.
Reevaluating the Bundesbank's gold to market value would create 40 billion marks in windfall profits for Bonn.
Meanwhile silver was quiet, following gold but never straying from a narrow range. COMEX July silver settled 2.0 cents firmer at $4.858 an ounce, traded $4.87 to $4.835.
Gold and silver volumes were 35,000 and 9,000 respectively.
The white metals ended barely changed in light dealings.
"This is pretty impressive bearing in mind the strength of the yen," a dealer said.
A strong Japanese currency would tend to put downward pressure on dollar denominated palladium and platinum futures, as so much of the white metals are traded in yen.
Dealers were still waiting to see when the delayed 1997 export shipments of Russian platinum and palladium actually start.
July NYMEX platinum settled 10 cents firmer at $393.90 an ounce, traded $396.80 to $392.00. June NYMEX palladium went out 65 cents weaker at $173.25 an ounce.
